questions.q: In the original DDPM formulation, what does the parameter $\beta_t$ represent?
options: The standard deviation of the Gaussian noise
The variance of the noise added at step $t$
The log-SNR of the current step
The mean of the data distribution
questions.answer: The variance of the noise added at step $t$
questions.why: The lesson explicitly states: '$\beta_t$ is the variance of the noise added at step $t$. This is the "noise schedule."'

questions.q: According to the lesson, why is the closed-form solution $x_t = \sqrt{\bar{\alpha}_t} x_0 + \sqrt{1 - \bar{\alpha}_t} \epsilon$ crucial for training efficiency?
options: It allows the model to skip steps and sample $x_t$ directly from $x_0$ for any $t$
It eliminates the need for a neural network entirely
It ensures the noise level remains constant throughout the process
It converts the stochastic process into a deterministic ODE
questions.answer: It allows the model to skip steps and sample $x_t$ directly from $x_0$ for any $t$
questions.why: The text states: 'This allows us to sample $x_t$ directly from $x_0$ for any $t$, which is crucial for training efficiency.'

questions.q: Why is it incorrect to assume the forward diffusion process is reversible without training a model?
questions.answer: Because the noise is random, so you must train a model to predict the noise based on the noisy input rather than simply subtracting the added noise.
questions.why: The 'Common mistakes' section states: 'You cannot simply subtract the noise you added. The noise is random. You must train a model to *predict* the noise based on the noisy input.'
